lines.text: Tiffany polished a diamond with meteorite dust.
In 1891, a scientist reported diamonds inside an Arizona meteorite.
lines.say: In eighteen ninety one, a scientist reported diamonds inside an Arizona meteorite.

lines.text: Cutting one slice took a day and a half and broke chisels.
The emery wheel meant to polish it was ruined.
In 1893, George Kunz of Tiffany tested the black grains.
lines.say: In eighteen ninety three, George Koonts of Tiffany tested the black grains.

lines.text: The test took place in Tiffany's pavilion at the Chicago World's Fair.
Tiffany's staff made a wheel that turned 2,500 times a minute.
lines.say: Tiffany's staff made a wheel that turned twenty five hundred times a minute.

lines.text: On the bare wheel, a diamond stayed unpolished after five minutes.
Then they charged the wheel with meteorite dust mixed with oil.
A diamond face was polished in about three minutes.

post.caption: Tiffany polished a diamond with meteorite dust. In 1891, a scientist reported diamonds inside an Arizona meteorite. Cutting one slice took a day and a half and broke chisels, and the wheel meant to polish it was ruined. In 1893, George Kunz of Tiffany tested the black grains in Tiffany's diamond cutting pavilion at the Chicago World's Fair. On a new wheel turning 2,500 times a minute, a diamond stayed unpolished after five minutes. When the wheel was coated with meteorite dust mixed with oil, a diamond face was polished in about three minutes.
